newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Tellus in shake-up after losses.
newsitem.headline: China's Tellus in shake-up after losses.

text.p: China's Shenzhen Tellus Holdings Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had replaced all seven of its board directors to try to turn the company around after two years of losses.
Tellus had removed Fang Shimao from his post as chairman and appointed Cheng Hongming as his successor, the company said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
Fang's removal came after the company posted heavy losses in both 1995 and 1996, a Tellus spokeswoman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Fang was not immediately available for comment.

Tellus, which is involved in industry, real estate and foreign trade, posted a net loss of 187.55 million yuan ($22.6 million) for 1996 against a net loss of 20.36 million yuan for 1995 under international accounting standards.

The reshuffle came soon after state-owned Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Development (Group) Co bought 159.588 million unlisted state shares, or 72.4 percent of Tellus's outstanding shares, from Shenzhen Investment Management Co under the Shenzhen city government.
Four of the seven new directors, who were elected by Tellus shareholders at a meeting on June 8, come from the Shenzhen Development Group, the statement showed.
Tellus's new chairman Cheng, 53, is also the Communist Party secretary of Shenzhen Development, it said.

"The new leadership is mulling plans to save Tellus, including the injection of some of Shenzhen Development's assets into the loss-maker," the Tellus spokeswoman said but declined to give further details.
Shareholders also approved a plan to forego a dividend for 1996 due to the losses.
